requirements.quote:
QUIC uses separate packet number spaces for each encryption level,
   except 0-RTT and all generations of 1-RTT keys use the same packet
   number space.
requirements.condition: When assigning packet numbers for encryption levels other than the stated 0-RTT/1-RTT exception
requirements.required_behavior: Use a separate packet number space for each encryption level.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not use one shared packet number space for distinct encryption levels outside the stated exception.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is stated.
requirements.why_checkable: An implementation's packet-number allocation and tracking can be inspected or exercised to verify that non-excepted encryption levels have distinct spaces.

requirements.quote:
QUIC uses separate packet number spaces for each encryption level,
   except 0-RTT and all generations of 1-RTT keys use the same packet
   number space.
requirements.condition: When assigning packet numbers to 0-RTT packets or to packets protected with any generation of 1-RTT keys
requirements.required_behavior: Use the same packet number space for 0-RTT and every generation of 1-RTT keys.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not create separate packet number spaces for 0-RTT versus 1-RTT or for different generations of 1-RTT keys.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is stated.
requirements.why_checkable: Packet-number state can be inspected across 0-RTT and successive 1-RTT key generations to confirm that all use one shared space.

requirements.quote:
Separate packet number spaces ensures that the
   acknowledgment of packets sent with one level of encryption will not
   cause spurious retransmission of packets sent with a different
   encryption level.
requirements.condition: When an acknowledgment is processed for packets sent at one encryption level
requirements.required_behavior: Keep acknowledgment and loss-processing state isolated so that packets in a different encryption level are not spuriously treated as requiring retransmission.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: The acknowledgment must not cause spurious retransmission of packets sent with a different encryption level.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is stated.
requirements.why_checkable: A trace with outstanding packets in multiple encryption levels can verify that acknowledging one level does not trigger retransmission decisions for another level.

requirements.quote:
Congestion control and round-trip time (RTT)
   measurement are unified across packet number spaces.
requirements.condition: When congestion-control state is updated for packets belonging to different packet number spaces
requirements.required_behavior: Apply one unified congestion-control regime across all packet number spaces.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not operate independent congestion-control regimes solely because packets belong to different packet number spaces.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is stated.
requirements.why_checkable: Congestion-window and bytes-in-flight updates can be traced across packet number spaces to determine whether they feed shared congestion-control state.

requirements.quote:
Congestion control and round-trip time (RTT)
   measurement are unified across packet number spaces.
requirements.condition: When RTT samples are obtained from packets belonging to different packet number spaces
requirements.required_behavior: Maintain unified RTT measurement across all packet number spaces.
requirements.forbidden_behavior: Do not maintain independent RTT estimators solely because samples belong to different packet number spaces.
requirements.error_behavior: No specific error response is stated.
requirements.why_checkable: RTT estimator updates can be traced using acknowledgments from multiple packet number spaces to verify that samples contribute to unified measurement state.
